overview.description: Clag (also known as Nominations) is a British card game that originated in the Royal Air Force during World War II. The name is an acronym for 'Clouds Low Aircraft Grounded'â€”reflecting when air crews played while waiting for suitable weather. It combines Oh Hell!-style exact bidding with 22 deals including 8 special deals with unique rules (No Trumps, Misere, Blind, Twos Wild, etc.).

history.origins: Clag originated in the British Royal Air Force during World War II. According to Taylor Foss, the name CLAG is an acronym for 'Clouds Low Aircraft Grounded'â€”air crews played this game while waiting for weather conditions suitable for flying. Also known as 'Clagg' or 'Cleg'.
timeline: Post-War: Spread through British card-playing circles
Present: Played by card game enthusiasts, particularly in UK
history.evolution: The game evolved from Oh Hell! by adding special deals with unique rules. The 22-deal structure with 8 special deals in the middle distinguishes it from simpler exact-bidding games.
history.cultural: Strongly associated with British military culture, particularly the RAF. The acronym name reflects the practical humor of service personnel.

setup.players: 4-7 players. Deal and play are clockwise.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, score pad for cumulative scoring.
setup.dealing: 22 deals total. Deals 1-7: 1-7 cards each. Deals 8-15: special deals, 7 cards each. Deals 16-22: 7-1 cards each. Trump determined by turning next card after deal (except special deals).

rules.objective: Players try to predict the exact number of tricks they will win in each deal. Over 22 deals (hand sizes 1–7, then eight special seven-card deals, then 7 down to 1), each player scores one point per trick won plus a 10-point bonus for making their bid exactly. The player with the highest cumulative score after all 22 deals wins.
rules.gameplay: 22 deals (1-7 cards, then 8 special deals, then 7-1). Bid exact tricks. Trump by turned card (except specials: No Trump, Misere, Blind, Twos Wild, etc). Follow suit. Dealer's bid restricted so total ≠ cards dealt. Score for making bid.
keyRules: Deals 1-7 and 16-22 are normal Oh Hell! deals
Deals 8-15 are special deals with unique rules
Dealer's bid restricted so total cannot equal cards dealt

strategy.basic: In normal deals, bid based on your hand strength. Remember the dealer restrictionâ€”if you're dealer, you may be forced into a difficult bid.
strategy.intermediate: Special deals require different strategies: In Misere, try to lose every trick. In Blind, bid conservatively. In Twos Wild, wild cards change hand valuation significantly.
strategy.advanced: Track cumulative scoresâ€”players behind may take more risks. In Dealer Calls Trumps, dealer has significant advantage. Coordinate play to cause ties in Highest Number deal.
tips: The dealer restriction (can't make total equal cards dealt) is crucialâ€”plan accordingly
In Misere, low cards are valuable; in normal deals, high cards are valuable
Twos Wild dramatically changes hand evaluationâ€”treat Twos as potentially any card

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.
